purpose: Pemetrexed is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of lung cancer, including non-small cell lung cancer and malignant pleural mesothelioma, which is a cancer affecting the lining of the lungs. It is sometimes used alone and sometimes combined with other chemotherapy drugs. Your doctor chose this medicine because it targets and helps slow down or stop the growth of cancer cells in your body.
how_it_works: Pemetrexed works by blocking certain vitamins that cancer cells need to grow and multiply, specifically folate. Think of it like cutting off the fuel supply that cancer cells rely on to copy themselves. Without this fuel, cancer cells cannot divide and spread as easily, which helps slow or stop the cancer from growing.
common_side_effects: Feeling very tired or weak, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, mouth sores or soreness, constipation or diarrhea, skin rash, low blood cell counts which can make you more prone to infections, bruising or bleeding more easily, and hair thinning. Your doctor will give you folic acid vitamins and a vitamin B12 shot before treatment to help reduce some of these side effects.
warnings: This medicine can seriously lower your blood cell counts, making it harder for your body to fight infections and increasing your risk of bleeding — contact your doctor right away if you have a fever, chills, or unusual bleeding. It can harm an unborn baby, so pregnancy must be avoided during treatment. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially anti-inflammatory pain relievers like ibuprofen. It can also cause serious kidney problems, so your kidney function will be checked regularly. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: Pemetrexed is given as an IV infusion (drip into a vein) by a nurse or doctor, usually once every 21 days (one cycle). The dose is calculated based on your height and weight. You will also need to take folic acid by mouth every day starting about a week before treatment, and you will receive a vitamin B12 injection every 9 weeks to help protect your body from certain side effects.
